correctness.rationale: Definitions and all boundary cases reconstructed from frozen RESULT.md. F(t)=2t−t log t has derivative log(e/t), F(1)=2. For a=max(0,x−r), b=min(1,x+r), ell=b−a, L=log(e/b), r<=ell<=2r for r<=1, and 0<=∫_a^b log(b/t)dt=ell+a log(a/b)<=ell, whence rL<=mu(B)<=4rL. b_R/b_r<=R/r yields mu(B_R)/mu(B_r)>=(R/r)/[4(1+log(R/r))]. Maximizing r^(1−lambda)log(e/r) for 0<=lambda<1 gives A_lambda=4e^(−lambda)/(1−lambda). Telescoping nested means with Holder yields sum S_{p,lambda}=Σ_{j>=0}(1+j log2)^(1/p)2^(−j(1−lambda)/p)<∞ for each fixed lambda<1, including p=1; top-scale mean controlled by mu(X)=2 and Lp. Minkowski proves the advertised norm inclusion. For lambda=0 target Morrey is Lp. Density>=1 and intervals have length>=r prove lower 1-regularity; mass comparison gives doubling<=8. At x=0, mu(B(0,r))/r=2−log r→∞, so upper 1-regularity and endpoint L_M^{p,1} membership of f=1 fail while f=1 has finite L_C norm. Finite test of 20000 independently generated (x,r,R) samples supports but does not prove mass bounds: minimum observed reverse-growth slack 3.49146 and maximum doubling ratio 2.85259; conclusions are analytic. No uniform lambda→1 bound is claimed.
residual_risks: Finite numerical sampling is illustrative, not an infinite proof.
No sharp optimal embedding constant is established; only boundedness for each fixed p and lambda.

evidence: Nakai 2006, definitions p.2, conditions (2.1)–(2.4) p.4 and Corollary 2.3 p.5: for finite doubling (X,d,mu), L_{p,phi}-Campanato coincides continuously with L_{p,phi}-Morrey when phi satisfies four shape/scale conditions and integral Phi(a,r)=∫_r^{2R0}phi(a,t)dt/t<=C phi(a,r). Setting phi(a,r)=r^(lambda/p)/mu(B(a,r))^(1/p) makes the Nakai seminorms precisely the submitted radius-normalized seminorms.

For 0<lambda<1, 1<=p<infinity: (2.1) follows from doubling and 2-scale radius powers; (2.2) holds with theta=1 because phi(r)/r=r^(lambda/p-1)/mu(B(r))^(1/p) decreases with r; (2.3) reduces exactly to ∫_0^r t^(lambda/p-1)dt=(p/lambda)r^(lambda/p), also for radii exceeding the diameter; (2.4) follows from B(a,r)⊂B(b,2r) for d(a,b)<=r and doubling. For r<=t<=1 the exact reverse-growth estimate mu(B(a,t))/mu(B(a,r)) >=(t/r)/[4(1+log(t/r))] gives phi(a,t)/phi(a,r)<=4^(1/p)(1+log(t/r))^(1/p)(t/r)^(-(1-lambda)/p); integrating dt/t is finite for each strict lambda. The bounded t∈[1,2R0] contribution is absorbed since phi(a,r)>=A_lambda^(-1/p) for r<=1, and all remaining r lie in a compact interval. Thus Nakai Corollary 2.3 directly yields the asserted continuous embedding for every 0<lambda<1. lambda=0 is L^p trivially; lambda=1 fails for f=1 by the elementary mass formula.
Stempak–Tao 2014, Section 3 and Remark 7, gives related generalized local/global frameworks but does not supply the decisive domination; Nakai Cor.2.3 does.
broader_coverage.reasoning: All of Nakai’s explicit hypotheses hold for the given log-density measure for each fixed 0<lambda<1. The older general sufficient criterion therefore covers the full claimed family of positive inclusions; its conclusion is not just analogous or qualitative.

originality.rationale: Scientific priority is defeated by the 2006 Nakai general equivalence theorem. The positive subcritical embedding is directly a specialization of its Corollary 2.3 after the exact parameter substitution phi(x,r)=r^(lambda/p)/mu(B(x,r))^(1/p); the submitted ball mass/reverse growth computations verify all the published hypotheses uniformly. The remaining lambda=0 and endpoint constant-function observations are elementary. Nakai did not explicitly publish this 2026 question or log-density example in the inspected theorem, but the audited claim is a mathematical consequence of the stronger prior result, so wording mismatch/newly phrased question cannot establish O. This is a scientific rejection, NOT a failure caused by inaccessible 2026 full text.
residual_risks: The Nakai theorem decisively covers the continuous embeddings for every 0<lambda<1; although it does not explicitly list the particular logarithmic density or later question, the required specialization is elementary and therefore cannot be claimed as an original theorem under the stated implication standard.

value.rationale: The proposed boundary example addresses a natural mathematical question: whether all strict-subcritical Campanato-to-Morrey embeddings force upper critical volume regularity. A finite nonatomic, compact, connected, doubling, lower-1-regular weight exhibiting a logarithmic defect is mathematically motivated; the sharp critical endpoint and quantified failure are substantive even though the embedding follows from a prior general theorem. This is potential explanatory value, not a claim of independent novelty, and no paper-sized theorem is required. The precise positive range and endpoint failure make a coherent natural counterexample rather than an arbitrary slice or tiny numerical gain.
residual_risks: As a new contribution the result has limited independent value because a 2006 general theorem already implies the central embedding; V=PASS does not rescue O=FAIL.
